description: council-forge standards-uplift timeline — the SSOT (single source of truth) of WHEN each governance standard / gate / discipline was introduced. Consumed read-only by standards_backaudit_dashboard.py to compute, per task, which standards were uplifted AFTER that task completed (its theoretical 'qualitative delta'). This timeline records WHEN a bar rose; it does NOT certify that any older task does or does not meet today's bar — that qualitative judgement is NOT machine-decidable (see the dashboard caveat). Each event's introduced_at is the committer instant (git log -1 --format=%cI <commit>), so same-day events are ordered by instant, never collapsed to a date.

maintenance.rule: Any task that introduces a NEW governance standard (a new guard, a new threshold, or anything in the dual-review / SSDF / fail-closed / dispatch / lifecycle / write-scope classes) MUST append one event to this timeline in the same change. This timeline is a LIVING SSOT, not a one-time snapshot: an un-recorded uplift makes every later back-audit under-count the qualitative delta of earlier tasks.

entry_format.introduced_at: ISO 8601 instant, evidenced by `git log -1 --format=%cI <commit>` (committer instant, +08:00)
entry_format.event: short human label of what was uplifted
entry_format.standard: the standard / threshold / discipline that became required at that instant
entry_format.ref: the introducing task id (e.g. TASK-1079) or PR anchor
entry_format.commit: the introducing commit short-sha (the %cI evidence source)
entry_format.category: exactly one of `categories` below (fail-closed controlled vocabulary)

events.event: sub-agent write-scope guard for dispatch wrappers
events.standard: Dispatch wrappers must declare a bounded write-scope; a sub-agent write outside the declared scope is a scope-drift / RACI violation and is guard-enforced.
Dispatch prompts must follow the token-cost discipline (docs/dispatch_prompt_discipline.md): bounded, structured, no unbounded context dumping.
Dispatch wrappers enforce a prompt-size bound, rejecting oversized prompts before dispatch.
Workflow must retrofit onto brownfield repos: a repo's own README/CLAUDE is preserved and classified brownfield-owned rather than overwritten.

events.event: adversarial dual-review gate established (commander policy) + P8 SSDLC roadmap
events.standard: Every plan must pass a codex+gemini adversarial dual-review (no blocking/critical findings) before any coding; security/crypto/auth plans additionally require a working-tree implementation-layer dual review.

events.event: P8-A SSDF mapping-integrity gate (NIST SP 800-218 v1.1)
events.standard: council-forge governance mechanisms are mapped to NIST SSDF practices and the mapping is integrity-gated (ssdf_mapping_validator); an unmapped or mis-mapped practice fails the gate.

events.event: P8-B secret-scan + SCA recognition, hardening, mapping, downstream templates
events.standard: Secret-scanning and software-composition-analysis gates are recognized, hardened, SSDF-mapped, and templated into downstream repos.
Security gates must fail closed: a missing or unparseable report version is a hard failure, never a silent pass.

events.event: P8-C advisory SAST (sast_gate + repo_security_scan sast + PW.7 partial)
events.standard: A static application security testing gate (advisory) is present and SSDF-mapped (PW.7 partial).
A software bill-of-materials gate (multi-ecosystem) is present and SSDF-mapped (PS.3).

events.event: P8-D vulnerability disclosure & response (security_txt_gate + SECURITY.md + IR runbook)
events.standard: A vulnerability-disclosure path (security.txt gate + SECURITY.md) and an incident-response runbook are present and SSDF-mapped (RV.1).
A release-integrity gate plus a snapshot manifest are present and SSDF-mapped (PS.2 partial).
Release-signing verification is implemented (PS.2 mechanism-implemented), strengthening release integrity beyond manifest snapshotting.

events.event: P8-E SSDF conformance dashboard + enablement SSOT (read-only, honest non-certification)
events.standard: A per-downstream SSDF mechanism-overlay dashboard (read-only, honest non-certification) and an enablement-matrix SSOT exist; mechanism presence is reported honestly and never conflated with enforcement.
